paper.title: GraphCast: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting
paper.authors: Remi Lam, Alvaro Sanchez-Gonzalez, Matthew Willson et al.

thesis: GraphCast is a key advance in accurate and efficient weather forecasting, and helps realize the promise of machine learning for modeling complex dynamical systems.

reconstruction.scope: abstract-level graph with retained full text

nodes.title: Research question
nodes.body: What does the reported model reveal when the target system is simulated?

nodes.title: Choose model and boundary conditions
nodes.body: Traditional numerical weather prediction uses increased compute resources to improve forecast accuracy, but cannot directly use historical weather data to improve the underlying model.

nodes.title: Run the numerical experiment
nodes.body: It predicts hundreds of weather variables, over 10 days at 0.25 degree resolution globally, in under one minute.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: We show that GraphCast significantly outperforms the most accurate operational deterministic systems on 90% of 1380 verification targets, and its forecasts support better severe event prediction, including tropical cyclones, atmospheric rivers, and extreme temperatures.

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: GraphCast is a key advance in accurate and efficient weather forecasting, and helps realize the promise of machine learning for modeling complex dynamical systems.
